solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dismay with end of aged relative

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of aged is taken

parts.note: an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by an elderly relation's death.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to dismay or dishearten them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Result of a good hand in game — run succeeded with it

parts.note: draughts is the board game known in the US as checkers
to man a stall or office is to run it
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
hip and with it both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A card player wins a game with a strong hand and the success follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' suggests cards, but it means handwriting or drawing skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmanship is skill in drawing, the product of a skilled hand with pencil or pen.

clue.text: University pressure? A stimulant is the answer

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a can mean per, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Stress at university might be solved by taking a pep pill.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine, which lifts mood and energy.

clue.text: I got mixed up with rum lot in trouble

indicators.note: being mixed up means put into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to falling in with a dodgy bunch and ending up in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great confusion or disturbance, a kind of trouble.

clue.text: TV programme in the main sent round with no changes made

indicators.note: the TV programme sits inside the reversed sea, so 'in' places one piece within the other
sending something round turns it back the other way, so the word for the main is read backwards

parts.note: the main is a literary name for the open sea
a sitcom is a situation comedy, a kind of TV programme

explanation.surface: A television show set at sea is sent out to viewers without any edits.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something as it comes means accepting it unaltered, just in the state it arrives.

clue.text: More than one star which was once used to navigate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large southern constellation, now split into several

definitions.text: which was once used to navigate
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Jason's ship in Greek myth, sailed by the Argonauts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Navigate' points to stars as guides, but the second sense is the ship itself that was sailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Argo Navis is a constellation of many stars, named after the legendary vessel of Jason and the Argonauts.

clue.text: Rising in singular haste

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
urgency is pressing haste

explanation.surface: Getting up in a rush, and alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt, and insurgency is an armed uprising against authority.

clue.text: Type of conifer company cleared out on one of the estates

indicators.note: clearing out a word empties its inside, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: the press is the Fourth Estate, alongside the traditional three estates of the realm

explanation.surface: A firm has stripped a plantation of its trees on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estates' looks like landed property, but it means the estates of the realm; the press is the Fourth Estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is an evergreen cone-bearing tree, one of the conifer family.

clue.text: I love very big problem coming up for dictator

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and nil is zero
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very big
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a huge emerging issue with a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini ruled Fascist Italy as Il Duce, an example of an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: New growth starting by fruit just come out with it

parts.note: a shoot is new growth on a plant
starting by something is starting from the thing, so the words give 'from the'
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A gardener sees a fresh sprout appearing beside a fruit that has just emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plant description; a rose hip is the red fruit of a rose, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot from the hip is to speak bluntly and impulsively, saying what one thinks without preparation.

clue.text: What could be spears in a box — a blow not being all there

parts.note: to spar is to box, as in a practice bout

indicators.note: something not all there is incomplete, so the word for the blow loses its final letter

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind

explanation.surface: Spears are packed in a box, and someone is struck by a confusing blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spears' looks like weapons, but asparagus is eaten as spears, the young shoots of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus shoots are sold and cooked as 'spears', so spears could be this vegetable.

clue.text: White brandy is in per cent over

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the abbreviation for per cent

parts.note: PC is the standard abbreviation for per cent
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A spirit's alcohol strength is quoted in per cent, and it is above a certain figure.
explanation.walkthrough: PISCO is a colourless grape brandy from Peru and Chile.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisco is a clear, unaged grape spirit, a South American white brandy.

clue.text: Fierce woman knocking alcohol back — concerning

indicators.note: knocking back a drink means downing it, but here with 'back' it says the drink's name is read backwards
together with 'knocking', back says the word for alcohol is turned around

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or informally any alcoholic drink
on can mean concerning, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman is gulping down drink, perhaps worryingly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Gorgons were monstrous women; the name is used for any fearsome, formidable female.

clue.text: Look to return in army post where duty is relaxed.

indicators.note: the reversed look is placed inside the army post

parts.note: a fort is a fortified army post

indicators.note: returning sends the word back the way it came, so the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to go back and check in at a base where military duty is less strict.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'duty' a soldier's work; the definition means customs duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A free port is a harbour where imported goods are exempt from customs taxes, so the levy is waived there.

clue.text: Drive recorded debt with crafty way fake news appears?

parts.note: to spur is to drive on, urge
an IOU is a written note acknowledging a debt
sly means crafty

explanation.surface: A campaign driven by unpaid debts and cunning spreads false stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake news is false, so it presents itself in a bogus, counterfeit manner.

clue.text: Spell failure for this shooting style?

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a lapse is a failure or slip

explanation.surface: A spell that goes wrong might suit a particular way of photographing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' is filming, not firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse filming captures frames at long intervals so slow change plays back quickly, a technique of shooting footage.

clue.text: Chap who finally encountered Queen in Tube under some pressure?

parts.note: man is a chap

indicators.note: finally means take only the last letter

parts.note: met means encountered
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A man finally met the Queen on the London Underground in a stressful moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is a glass tube that measures pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A manometer is a U-shaped instrument for measuring fluid pressure, a gauge working under pressure.

clue.text: Captain dropping very soft sportsman in Winter Olympics

indicators.note: dropping something means leaving it out, so the musical marking is removed from the word for captain

parts.note: a skipper is a captain of a ship or team
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A team captain is left out of a gentle competitor's line-up at the Winter Games.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing events such as downhill and slalom are central to the Winter Olympics, so a skier competes there.

clue.text: Second fine fabric artist

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'
net is a fine open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A painter is described as the next one to work in delicate cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Little fish: young child has swapped ring for one

indicators.note: having swapped something means it has been exchanged, so the ring letter is taken out of the child's word
for names what the ring is swapped for, the letter standing for one going in its place

parts.note: a toddler is a young child learning to walk
O is ring-shaped
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A toddler trades a ring for a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is British informal for a very small fish such as a stickleback or minnow.

clue.text: Concerning swindle, company is to check again

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a con is a swindle
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A firm is under investigation for fraud and must audit its accounts once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconfirm something is to verify it a second time, which is checking it again.

clue.text: Roving about domain?

indicators.note: roving letters wander about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone wanders all over their territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a nomadic life is one of roving about the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic means wandering with no fixed home, moving from place to place across a region.

clue.text: Try to sound important? Pardon me, that's wrong

indicators.note: saying the letters are wrong means they are in a faulty order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a pompous speaker with a polite 'Pardon me, that's wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually to impress people, an attempt to seem significant.

clue.text: Bond's enemies succeeded — runs into snare

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for snare

parts.note: a mesh is a net or snare, as in caught in its meshes
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: James Bond's foes do well when he blunders into a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: SMERSH was the Soviet counter-intelligence agency that serves as the villains' organisation in Fleming's novels about the spy James Bond.

clue.text: Concerning about impossible flight path

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for concerning surrounds the other piece

parts.note: re means concerning
out means impossible, ruled out, as in 'that option is out'

explanation.surface: Someone worries about an escape that can't be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape, but it is an aircraft's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a course or way taken, and an aircraft's flight path is its route.

clue.text: Struggle between two parties of right and left

parts.note: a due is something one has a right to

explanation.surface: A contest between two political parties of right and left wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests politics; here it means the two people fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two opponents, a contest of two sides.

clue.text: House has permit rejected for commercial accommodation

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word for permit is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A house's planning permission is turned down when it is meant to be used as a business lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a business offering paid rooms to guests, lodging run for profit.

clue.text: Small sum we might invest in American prospector

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a sum we might invest is our money, and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A modest amount could be put into an American gold prospector's venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Old prospectors in Alaska and the Yukon carried sourdough starter for bread, and the name stuck to them.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American usage a sourdough is an old-timer prospector or settler of the far north.

clue.text: Representation changes area to old city used by pirates

indicators.note: the representation changes one of its letters, so the area abbreviation is taken out
to names the replacement, the old abbreviation, that goes in where the area letter was

parts.note: a portrayal is a representation or depiction

explanation.surface: A depiction alters its view of a district, showing a historic town once home to buccaneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old city' reads as one phrase, but 'old' only supplies the O that replaces the area's A.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Royal in Jamaica was a notorious seventeenth-century haven for buccaneers before an earthquake sank much of it.

clue.text: Cortege, oddly quiet and slow movement

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A funeral procession moves strangely silently and slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and stealthily, and a creep is that kind of slow progress.
